findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SpanFlusher silently discards the buffer argument from the factory and constructs bare SpansBuffer(shards) instances per process, so record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() run against default-constructed buffers instead of the factory-configured one; the dead parameter on the constructor is itself a smell.

[BUG] The tag key is "shards" in metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", ...) while every other tag in the same loop uses "shard", so dashboards grouping by shard drop the wait_produce series.

[BUG] In thread mode, _ensure_processes_alive catches (ValueError, AttributeError), skips killing the thread, then spawns a second thread polling the same shards, causing duplicate production of every span from those shards until consumer restart.

[BUG] In join(), when the deadline expires the outer for breaks, skipping process.terminate() for the current and remaining processes, leaking spawn processes that hold Redis connections and continue polling/producing after join() returns.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing calls it (the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards directly) — and should be deleted; its per-shard granularity is illusory since it restarts the whole process.

[ADVISORY] The core new logic of this PR — per-process health monitoring, restart counting, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS escalation, and multi-process backpressure — has no test coverage; the new tests only exercise construction, so restart-path regressions ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] test_basic depends on a wall-clock time.sleep(0.1) for flusher threads to observe the drift change, but monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", ...) patches it globally to a no-op, so the test passes only by accident of thread scheduling and will flake intermittently on slow CI.

[ADVISORY] The --flusher-processes option is added only to the ingest-spans entry, so any other wiring path silently gets None → one process per shard, unbounded by the operator-set limit, if the option list and factory drift.

[BUG] Inconsistent shard tag keys in flusher metrics: `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` while `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`, so dashboards grouping `spans.buffer.flusher.*` by `shard` silently drop the `wait_produce` series, breaking produce-vs-wait correlation.

[BUG] The added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_consumer.py is inert because the test monkeypatches global `time.sleep` to a no-op, so the assertion after `step.join()` depends on thread-scheduling luck rather than the added wait — flaky or falsely-passing verification.

[ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` has no call sites in the diff, leaving a stale single-shard restart entry point that diverges from the actual `_ensure_processes_alive` full-process restart, making future changes to restart semantics riskier.

[ADVISORY] No test coverage for the new per-process health/restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` (crash detection, hang detection via `process_healthy_since`, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` counting, `RuntimeError` consumer-restart path), so regressions in restart bookkeeping ship silently.

[ADVISORY] In `join`, when the deadline expires, `break` exits the loop before `terminate()` runs for remaining processes, leaving late spawn-mode flusher processes alive holding Redis connections and Kafka producers after shutdown timeout.

[ADVISORY] `--flusher-processes 0` is silently coerced to one process per shard via the `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback, giving operators maximum parallelism instead of a validation error when they intended to disable it.

[ADVISORY] `shard_tag` becomes a comma-joined list when a process covers many shards (e.g. `"1,2,3,4"`), causing metric cardinality explosion across rebalance permutations; a per-process-index tag would bound cardinality.

[ADVISORY] The backpressure metric `spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure` is incremented inside the per-process loop, so one submit can fire the counter N times before a single `MessageRejected`, inflating the backpressure rate metric up to flusher-process-count-fold.

[BUG] CLAUDE.md adds unrelated isinstance/hasattr guidance documentation under a PR about span-buffer multiprocess enhancement — scope drift with no traceability, risking the doc change being lost or dragged along in future reverts

[BUG] `_create_process_for_shard` in flusher.py is dead code with no call sites and no tests, duplicating process-index lookup logic and risking divergence from `_ensure_processes_alive` restart mechanism

[ADVISORY] `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` falsy-coercion silently turns max_processes=0 into maximum parallelism (one process per shard) instead of raising or clamping, with no validation at any config layer

[ADVISORY] Inconsistent metric tag key drift: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}` (plural) while `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}`, preventing per-shard joins across flusher phases

[ADVISORY] Dead guard `if not process: continue` in flusher.py — processes dict values are never falsy and `is_alive()` already handles dead processes; the guard implies an absent-process state that cannot occur

[ADVISORY] Constructor's `buffer` argument is no longer stored as `self.buffer` while still accepted and used only for shard-count computation, silently breaking callers/tests that access `flusher.buffer` with no deprecation path

[BUG] Single shared current_drift Value is written by every flusher process with last-writer-wins semantics, so a fast process can overwrite a slower process's drift, causing the committer to commit Kafka offsets for segments still unflushed in Redis and permanently losing spans on crash/rebalance; should be min-across-processes or per-process aggregation with a lock

[BUG] No validation on flusher_processes before computing num_processes; a negative or zero value results in zero flusher processes running, causing silent unbounded Redis fill with no error, metric, or recovery

[ADVISORY] Hot-path fan-out regression in submit(): record_stored_segments and get_memory_info are now called once per flusher process per message, multiplying Redis round-trips (e.g. 32x with 32 shards) on the high-volume ingest path

[ADVISORY] Silent default behavior change: constructing ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without flusher_processes now defaults to one process per shard instead of one, causing an N× process-count increase for existing non-CLI callers

[ADVISORY] Metric tag-key drift: spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged with 'shards' while related metrics use 'shard', causing dashboards/alerts keyed on the shard tag to silently drop the wait_produce series

[ADVISORY] In produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, the hang restart path cannot kill the hung thread but unconditionally spawns a replacement, leading to two threads polling the same shards and producing overlapping/duplicate segments in test/embedded deployments

[BUG] Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use tag key "shard" but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses "shards", so dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` silently drop wait_produce data and the two latency series cannot be joined (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:193)

[BUG] Memory backpressure check now iterates every per-process buffer calling `get_memory_info()` on each — a consumer with 32 shards performs 32 Redis round-trips on every `submit()` call instead of 1, a hot-path latency regression from 1 Redis call to N exactly when Redis is under memory pressure (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:298-302)

[ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` has no call site in the diff and duplicates the shard→process lookup that `_ensure_processes_alive` already performs, creating two plausible entry points for the next maintainer changing restart policy (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:139-144)

[ADVISORY] Unrelated Python style-guide edit (hasattr vs isinstance for unions) smuggled into CLAUDE.md in a PR about span-buffer multiprocess health monitoring, making the change unreviewable by anyone filtering for flusher code (CLAUDE.md:448-457)

[ADVISORY] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` silently rewrites an explicit `0` into one-process-per-shard (maximum parallelism) instead of erroring on the invalid configuration, so a `--flusher-processes 0` typo spawns N processes per consumer (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53)

The new --flusher-processes CLI option is unbounded above, allowing an operator to pass a huge process count value (though it is clamped by len(buffer.assigned_shards) and is a resource-tuning concern rather than a vulnerability)

[BUG] In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-62, the test monkeypatches time.sleep globally, making its own time.sleep(0.1) synchronization call a no-op; the claimed synchronization never happens and the test passes only via a flaky race with step.join().

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit in test_consumer.py:82-119 asserts only private attributes and implementation structure (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, process_to_shards_map bookkeeping) without submitting messages or asserting flushed output, so a wiring regression in _create_process_for_shards would ship green.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten crash/hang detection and restart logic in flusher.py:218-266 (_ensure_processes_alive: restart counters, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, isinstance kill guard, per-shard metrics.incr fan-out) has no test exercising it.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten join() timeout logic in flusher.py:326-345 is untested for the multi-process case: the early break can leave remaining processes un-terminated, and negative remaining_time can skip terminating any process, risking shutdown hangs or leaked processes.

[ADVISORY] main() in flusher.py:126 gains a required positional shards parameter, and tests only use produce_to_pipe (threading.Thread path), so the mp_context.Process spawn branch including pickling of SpansBuffer and the new shards argument has zero test coverage.

[ADVISORY] The changed assertion in test_flusher.py:83 (assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())) is weaker than the code it replaced and never asserts MessageRejected is raised by submit() under sustained backpressure, so a regression reading the wrong process's flag still passes.

[BUG] `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `process.kill()` then immediately creates a new process for the same shards, but kill() is asynchronous, so the old process continues its poll/produce loop on the same shards until the signal is delivered while the new process also reads the same Redis segments — causing the same span segments to be read and produced to INGEST_SPANS twice during every restart window

[ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is dead code that, if invoked by a future caller, creates an additional process for the shard's process-index and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without killing the old entry, leaving two uncoordinated processes flushing the same Redis segments with duplicate span production invisible to health-checking

[ADVISORY] The restart path replaces `self.buffers[process_index]` with a brand-new `SpansBuffer(shards)`, discarding all in-memory state of the killed buffer's shard set while `submit()` continues calling `record_stored_segments()` as if continuity were preserved — causing counters to be re-derived from zero on restart so consumers see counter drops and operators cannot distinguish `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` storms from real drift

[BUG] The `break` on `remaining_time <= 0` in flusher.py:330-345 exits the loop before `process.terminate()` runs for the current process, so flusher processes still alive past the deadline are never terminated; on shutdown, remaining spawn processes leak, keep polling Redis, hold Redis connections, and potentially double-produce segments after the consumer is replaced by a restart.

[ADVISORY] In `_ensure_processes_alive` restart path (flusher.py:244-262), the killed process is never `join()`ed before `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten, so SIGKILLed spawn processes become zombies until the parent reaps them, leaving one unreaped process per restart cycle over MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS.

[ADVISORY] In flusher.py:57, `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `flusher_processes=0` (or negative values) as falsy, so an operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` silently gets one process per shard with no validation or warning.

[ADVISORY] Hot-path Redis-call multiplication in submit (flusher.py:267-269): `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` now fan out to one call per shard-buffer per submit instead of one call total, increasing per-message latency linearly with the number of flusher processes.

[ADVISORY] Metric tag inconsistency and unbounded cardinality (flusher.py:181-207): `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use tag key `shard` while `wait_produce` uses `shards`, and the value is the joined shard list, breaking dashboards and creating combinatorial cardinality that inflates metric storage.

[ADVISORY] Dead/shadowed code path: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` (flusher.py:112-120) is never invoked anywhere — all call sites use `_create_process_for_shards` directly — and will diverge from the real path if mapping semantics change; it can be deleted with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] Dead guard in flusher.py:234-236: `if not process: continue` can never fire since Process/Thread objects are always truthy, misleading readers and silently skipping health checks for a process lost from `self.processes`, whose shards stop being flushed with no `flusher_unhealthy` metric emitted.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.__init__(buffer: SpansBuffer, ...)` no longer stores `self.buffer`, and `_create_process_for_shards` constructs fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances which are then used for `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` via `self.buffers`. That is a real design/maintenance concern (the passed-in buffer is only used for `assigned_shards`/process sizing), but the finding’s claim that this breaks “factory-configured” behavior or that the `buffer` parameter is dead is not fully verifiable from the diff (the parameter is still used, and we can’t see any extra configuration/state on `SpansBuffer`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In thread mode, _ensure_processes_alive catches (ValueError, AttributeError), skips killing the thread, then spawns a second thread polling the same shards, causing duplicate production of every span from those shards until consumer restart.

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is deemed unhealthy due to hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it attempts to kill only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so threads are not stopped. It then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, which starts a new thread for the same shards and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`, leaving the old (still-alive) thread running and polling/producing concurrently for the same shards, which can lead to duplicate production until shutdown/restart.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code — nothing calls it (the restart path calls _create_process_for_shards directly) — and should be deleted; its per-shard granularity is illusory since it restarts the whole process.

adjudication.rationale: In the new SpanFlusher implementation, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added but there is no call site in the diff. The restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts by `process_index` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` and never uses per-shard restart. As written, `_create_process_for_shard` would also restart the entire process for that shard group, so the “per-shard” granularity is misleading. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue (dead/unused code), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The core new logic of this PR — per-process health monitoring, restart counting, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS escalation, and multi-process backpressure — has no test coverage; the new tests only exercise construction, so restart-path regressions ship undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `SpanFlusher`—multi-process creation and shard mapping (`process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `buffers`), per-process health/backpressure state (`process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`), and the new restart/escalation logic in `_ensure_processes_alive()` (including `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` handling and per-shard metrics). The added/updated tests don’t exercise those paths: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts construction-time properties (counts and shard distribution) and never simulates a dead/hung process or restart; `test_flusher.py` change only checks `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` without validating multi-process backpressure rejection behavior (`MessageRejected`) or restarts. So regressions in restart/health/backpressure logic could ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The --flusher-processes option is added only to the ingest-spans entry, so any other wiring path silently gets None → one process per shard, unbounded by the operator-set limit, if the option list and factory drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires the new Click option `--flusher-processes` only into the `ingest-spans` consumer entry (`src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`), while the underlying factory/strategy now supports `flusher_processes` (`ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` and `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`). When `flusher_processes` is not provided, `SpanFlusher` defaults `max_processes` to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one process per shard), so any construction path that doesn’t pass the new parameter (or expose the CLI option) will not be bounded by an operator-set limit. The existence of other wiring paths isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s more of a completeness/drift concern than a confirmed runtime defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use the key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This is directly shown in the diff and will cause `wait_produce` series not to be grouped/filtered alongside the other per-shard metrics when dashboards/alerts expect a `shard` tag.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py` the diff adds a new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int): ...`, but all restart logic shown in the diff uses `_ensure_processes_alive()` which calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. There are no call sites for `_create_process_for_shard` in the diff, making it dead/unused code and a potential maintenance hazard if restart semantics evolve.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test coverage for the new per-process health/restart logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` (crash detection, hang detection via `process_healthy_since`, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` counting, `RuntimeError` consumer-restart path), so regressions in restart bookkeeping ship silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial per-process liveness/restart bookkeeping in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (iterating `self.processes`, using `process_healthy_since[...]` for hang detection, incrementing `self.process_restarts[...]`, killing/recreating a specific process, and raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). The new/updated tests (`test_flusher_processes_limit`, `test_basic`, and the backpressure assertion change) only validate process-count/shard distribution and backpressure dict behavior; they do not simulate a dead process, an unhealthy/hung process via `process_healthy_since`, or the repeated-crash path that triggers the `RuntimeError`. So the finding about missing test coverage for this new restart/health logic is accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `--flusher-processes 0` is silently coerced to one process per shard via the `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` fallback, giving operators maximum parallelism instead of a validation error when they intended to disable it.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `max_processes=0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Since the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is a plain `int` with no validation, an operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` would be silently ignored and result in `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becoming `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e., maximum parallelism instead of 0/disabled or an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `shard_tag` becomes a comma-joined list when a process covers many shards (e.g. `"1,2,3,4"`), causing metric cardinality explosion across rebalance permutations; a per-process-index tag would bound cardinality.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `shard_tag` is set to `",".join(map(str, shards))` and then used in metric tags (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`). Since `shards` can be a varying list per process (based on rebalance/distribution), this can create many distinct tag values like "1,2" vs "2,1" etc., increasing metric cardinality. This is a monitoring/operational concern introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backpressure metric `spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure` is incremented inside the per-process loop, so one submit can fire the counter N times before a single `MessageRejected`, inflating the backpressure rate metric up to flusher-process-count-fold.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the backpressure check loops over `self.process_backpressure_since.values()`, but as soon as any process exceeds the threshold it does `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")` and immediately `raise MessageRejected()` (see the new loop around lines ~264-287). That means a single `submit` call can increment the metric at most once, not N times. The finding’s claimed N-fold inflation per submit is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] CLAUDE.md adds unrelated isinstance/hasattr guidance documentation under a PR about span-buffer multiprocess enhancement — scope drift with no traceability, risking the doc change being lost or dragged along in future reverts

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation addition in CLAUDE.md about using isinstance() vs hasattr() for union types, while the rest of the PR changes span-buffer flusher multiprocessing behavior and related tests/options. This is scope drift (unconnected change in the same PR) and can complicate review/reverts or cause the doc change to be inadvertently reverted later. It’s not a runtime defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `_create_process_for_shard` in flusher.py is dead code with no call sites and no tests, duplicating process-index lookup logic and risking divergence from `_ensure_processes_alive` restart mechanism

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly introduced but has no call sites in the shown diff (all restarts happen via `_ensure_processes_alive()` calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). No tests reference `_create_process_for_shard`. This is dead code and it duplicates the shard→process_index lookup already implicit in `_ensure_processes_alive` via `process_to_shards_map`, creating a maintainability risk if restart logic changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` falsy-coercion silently turns max_processes=0 into maximum parallelism (one process per shard) instead of raising or clamping, with no validation at any config layer

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the new config parameter is assigned via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This is falsy-coercion: if a caller passes `max_processes=0` (possible since the new click option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation/min), it will silently become `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and thus enable maximum parallelism instead of honoring 0 or rejecting it. This is a real behavioral bug introduced by the diff (an unintended meaning for an explicit user-supplied value).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Inconsistent metric tag key drift: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}` (plural) while `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}`, preventing per-shard joins across flusher phases

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys for the same shard identifier: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards` (plural). This is a real, diff-grounded observability issue that would hinder correlating/joining metrics across phases by a consistent tag key, but it doesn’t constitute a functional correctness defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead guard `if not process: continue` in flusher.py — processes dict values are never falsy and `is_alive()` already handles dead processes; the guard implies an absent-process state that cannot occur

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the guard `if not process: continue` is indeed redundant given how `self.processes` is populated (`_create_process_for_shards` always stores a started `multiprocessing.Process` or `threading.Thread`). But this is a minor cleanup/style nit rather than a substantive review issue or defect; the diff shows no path where `process` could be falsy (e.g., `None`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Constructor's `buffer` argument is no longer stored as `self.buffer` while still accepted and used only for shard-count computation, silently breaking callers/tests that access `flusher.buffer` with no deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the incoming `buffer: SpansBuffer` is no longer stored as `self.buffer` (the prior `self.buffer = buffer` line is removed). The constructor still accepts `buffer` and uses it to read `buffer.assigned_shards` for `max_processes`/shard-to-process mapping, but thereafter it creates new per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances stored in `self.buffers`. This is a backward-incompatible attribute/API change that would break any callers/tests expecting `flusher.buffer` to exist, though no such usage is shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Single shared current_drift Value is written by every flusher process with last-writer-wins semantics, so a fast process can overwrite a slower process's drift, causing the committer to commit Kafka offsets for segments still unflushed in Redis and permanently losing spans on crash/rebalance; should be min-across-processes or per-process aggregation with a lock

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a single shared `self.current_drift = mp_context.Value("i", 0)` that is passed into every flusher worker via `_create_process_for_shards(... args=(..., self.current_drift, ...))`, but the provided diff snippet does not show any worker writing to `current_drift` (only tests mutate it) nor any committer logic that would use it to advance commits. Therefore the specific claim about “every flusher process writes it”, “last-writer-wins”, and “committer can commit offsets for unflushed segments causing permanent loss” is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] No validation on flusher_processes before computing num_processes; a negative or zero value results in zero flusher processes running, causing silent unbounded Redis fill with no error, metric, or recovery

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not support the claim that `flusher_processes` <= 0 results in “zero flusher processes running” and silent Redis fill. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and will fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so it will not create 0 processes. A negative value is truthy and would make `self.num_processes` negative (`min(negative, len(...))`), which would likely crash during shard mapping (empty `process_to_shards_map` then KeyError), not silently run with no flusher processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hot-path fan-out regression in submit(): record_stored_segments and get_memory_info are now called once per flusher process per message, multiplying Redis round-trips (e.g. 32x with 32 shards) on the high-volume ingest path

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()` the diff changes single-buffer calls into a loop over all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and similarly aggregates `get_memory_info()` from every buffer (flusher.py around `submit`). This means each submitted message now triggers N calls where N = `len(self.buffers)` (i.e., number of flusher processes), whereas previously it was exactly one (`self.buffer...`). Whether those calls translate to Redis round-trips isn’t shown in the diff, but the fan-out/multiplicative work per message is directly introduced here and can be a meaningful hot-path performance concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Silent default behavior change: constructing ProcessSpansStrategyFactory without flusher_processes now defaults to one process per shard instead of one, causing an N× process-count increase for existing non-CLI callers

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a default behavior change: `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` adds `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes it to `SpanFlusher(..., max_processes=self.flusher_processes)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so when callers omit `flusher_processes` (i.e., `None`), it now spawns `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` processes/threads via `_create_processes()`. Previously the flusher created a single process/thread via `_create_process()`. This is a silent scaling/resource behavior change for non-CLI callers, but not a directly verifiable correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Metric tag-key drift: spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce is tagged with 'shards' while related metrics use 'shard', causing dashboards/alerts keyed on the shard tag to silently drop the wait_produce series

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, related metrics use inconsistent tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This is diff-grounded and can break shard-keyed dashboards/alerts by splitting series across different tag keys, though it doesn't directly affect runtime correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In produce_to_pipe (thread) mode, the hang restart path cannot kill the hung thread but unconditionally spawns a replacement, leading to two threads polling the same shards and producing overlapping/duplicate segments in test/embedded deployments

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is deemed unhealthy (either `not process.is_alive()` or `hang` based on `process_healthy_since`), it always calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` to spawn a replacement. However, the “kill” step is guarded by `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, so in `produce_to_pipe` mode (where workers are `threading.Thread` per `_create_process_for_shards`), the hung thread cannot be terminated and is not otherwise stopped/joined before a new thread for the same `shards` is started. This can result in multiple live threads for the same shard set polling/producing concurrently (or one hung + one active), which matches the finding’s core concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use tag key "shard" but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses "shards", so dashboards/alerts grouped by `shard` silently drop wait_produce data and the two latency series cannot be joined (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:193)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses a different tag key ("shards"). This is a verifiable inconsistency introduced in `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py` and would cause metric series to be split across tag dimensions, breaking shard-grouped dashboards/alerts and preventing joins between related series.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Memory backpressure check now iterates every per-process buffer calling `get_memory_info()` on each — a consumer with 32 shards performs 32 Redis round-trips on every `submit()` call instead of 1, a hot-path latency regression from 1 Redis call to N exactly when Redis is under memory pressure (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:298-302)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the memory backpressure section changed from a single `memory_infos = list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` to iterating `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`. Since `self.buffers` is populated per flusher process (`_create_process_for_shards` creates a `SpansBuffer(shards)` and stores it), the number of `get_memory_info()` invocations per `submit()` can scale with `self.num_processes` (which defaults to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`), potentially increasing Redis calls from 1 to many. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/latency concern, but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` has no call site in the diff and duplicates the shard→process lookup that `_ensure_processes_alive` already performs, creating two plausible entry points for the next maintainer changing restart policy (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:139-144)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` (calls `_create_process_for_shards` after searching `process_to_shards_map`), but there is no call site for it anywhere in the shown diff. Restart logic is handled directly inside `_ensure_processes_alive()` using the same `process_index -> shards` mapping, so this helper is currently unused and duplicates the shard→process lookup logic, increasing maintenance surface without affecting runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Unrelated Python style-guide edit (hasattr vs isinstance for unions) smuggled into CLAUDE.md in a PR about span-buffer multiprocess health monitoring, making the change unreviewable by anyone filtering for flusher code (CLAUDE.md:448-457)

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation/style-guide change in CLAUDE.md adding guidance about `hasattr()` vs `isinstance()` for union types (new lines around 445+). This is orthogonal to the PR’s functional changes in `SpanFlusher` multiprocessing/health monitoring and can reasonably be considered scope creep that makes the PR harder to review when filtering for flusher-related files.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` silently rewrites an explicit `0` into one-process-per-shard (maximum parallelism) instead of erroring on the invalid configuration, so a `--flusher-processes 0` typo spawns N processes per consumer (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the new line `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `max_processes=0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This then feeds into `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, resulting in one-process-per-shard (maximum parallelism) rather than rejecting/handling an invalid 0 value. Since the CLI adds `--flusher-processes` as an `int` with no validation against 0, a `--flusher-processes 0` typo could trigger spawning N processes per consumer as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new --flusher-processes CLI option is unbounded above, allowing an operator to pass a huge process count value (though it is clamped by len(buffer.assigned_shards) and is a resource-tuning concern rather than a vulnerability)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new click.Option for `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no upper bound or lower-bound validation (e.g., `IntRange`), so an operator can pass an arbitrarily large number. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, this value is effectively clamped via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so it likely won’t actually spawn that many processes, making it more of an operational/UX/resource-tuning concern than a correctness/security defect. The finding is therefore real and grounded, but not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-62, the test monkeypatches time.sleep globally, making its own time.sleep(0.1) synchronization call a no-op; the claimed synchronization never happens and the test passes only via a flaky race with step.join().

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` near the top, patching the global `time.sleep` function. The newly added synchronization call `time.sleep(0.1)` (after the second `step.poll()`) therefore becomes a no-op, so the intended “give flusher threads time to process” delay never occurs. That makes the test rely on timing/races (e.g., whatever happens before/during `step.join()`), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit in test_consumer.py:82-119 asserts only private attributes and implementation structure (len(flusher.processes), max_processes, num_processes, process_to_shards_map bookkeeping) without submitting messages or asserting flushed output, so a wiring regression in _create_process_for_shards would ship green.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit` (new test in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`), the assertions validate only internal/private structure (`len(flusher.processes)`, `flusher.max_processes`, `flusher.num_processes`, and `process_to_shards_map` shard counts) after `create_with_partitions(...)`. The test never submits any messages to the strategy nor asserts any produced/flushed output via `messages.append`, so a functional wiring regression in `_create_process_for_shards` / per-shard `SpansBuffer` usage could still pass while breaking actual flushing behavior. This is a specific test-quality gap introduced by the diff rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten crash/hang detection and restart logic in flusher.py:218-266 (_ensure_processes_alive: restart counters, RuntimeError after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, isinstance kill guard, per-shard metrics.incr fan-out) has no test exercising it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially rewrites flusher restart/health logic from a single `self.process` to multiple `self.processes` with per-process health/backpressure state and restart counters in `_ensure_processes_alive()` (new loop, per-shard metrics fan-out, `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError, conditional `kill()` only for `multiprocessing.Process`). The tests added/modified only cover process-count limiting and shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure value storage (`test_flusher` change), but none simulate a dead process (`is_alive() == False`), a hang (`healthy_since` stale), restart counter increments/exhaustion, or verify the new RuntimeError path. So the finding is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten join() timeout logic in flusher.py:326-345 is untested for the multi-process case: the early break can leave remaining processes un-terminated, and negative remaining_time can skip terminating any process, risking shutdown hangs or leaked processes.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()` (flusher.py ~326-345), the new per-process loop can `break` when `remaining_time <= 0` before reaching the `terminate()` call for the current or subsequent processes. That means if the deadline is exceeded (or already exceeded after `next_step.join(timeout)`), the method can exit without terminating some/all still-alive multiprocessing processes, unlike the prior single-process logic which always reached `terminate()` after the wait loop. This can leak processes or hang shutdown in the multi-process case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] main() in flusher.py:126 gains a required positional shards parameter, and tests only use produce_to_pipe (threading.Thread path), so the mp_context.Process spawn branch including pickling of SpansBuffer and the new shards argument has zero test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SpanFlusher.main` to require a new positional `shards: list[int]` argument and updates `_create_process_for_shards` to always pass that via `args=(shards, ...)`. However, the tests shown (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`) instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` with `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which forces the `threading.Thread` path (`if self.produce_to_pipe is None: ... else: make_process = threading.Thread`). That means the `mp_context.Process`/`spawn` branch (including pickling the newly created `SpansBuffer(shards)` plus the new `shards` argument) has no coverage in this diff. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The changed assertion in test_flusher.py:83 (assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())) is weaker than the code it replaced and never asserts MessageRejected is raised by submit() under sustained backpressure, so a regression reading the wrong process's flag still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the test assertion from checking a single `flusher.backpressure_since.value` to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`. This is verifiably weaker: it no longer ties the expectation to a specific backpressure flag/process and would pass as long as any process sets its flag, even if the intended/triggering process is wrong. The claim about not asserting `MessageRejected` cannot be confirmed from the shown diff context (only the final assertion line is visible), but the reduced specificity of the assertion is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `process.kill()` then immediately creates a new process for the same shards, but kill() is asynchronous, so the old process continues its poll/produce loop on the same shards until the signal is delivered while the new process also reads the same Redis segments — causing the same span segments to be read and produced to INGEST_SPANS twice during every restart window

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a process/thread is deemed unhealthy it immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` after attempting to stop the old worker. The stop logic is incomplete/asynchronous: it calls `process.kill()` only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` and does not `join()`/wait for exit before starting the replacement; if the worker is a `threading.Thread` (when `produce_to_pipe is not None`), it isn’t killed at all, yet a new thread is still started for the same `shards`. This can result in two concurrent workers assigned to the same shards, both running `SpanFlusher.main(...)` and flushing/producing for the same shard set during the restart window (or indefinitely for threads).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is dead code that, if invoked by a future caller, creates an additional process for the shard's process-index and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without killing the old entry, leaving two uncoordinated processes flushing the same Redis segments with duplicate span production invisible to health-checking

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` the new helper `_create_process_for_shard` is not referenced anywhere in the diff (so it’s currently dead code), but its implementation (`_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`) will unconditionally start a new process/thread and then overwrite `self.processes[process_index]` without killing/joining the existing process for that index. That would leave the old process still running but no longer tracked by `_ensure_processes_alive()` (which iterates `self.processes.items()`), so health checks/restarts would ignore it. Because the restarted process is created with the same `shards` list, both processes would flush the same Redis shard segments, plausibly duplicating production. This is a real diff-grounded maintenance hazard, though not a currently exercised defect since there’s no caller shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The restart path replaces `self.buffers[process_index]` with a brand-new `SpansBuffer(shards)`, discarding all in-memory state of the killed buffer's shard set while `submit()` continues calling `record_stored_segments()` as if continuity were preserved — causing counters to be re-derived from zero on restart so consumers see counter drops and operators cannot distinguish `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` storms from real drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that on (re)start `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` always creates a fresh `SpansBuffer(shards)` and assigns it into `self.buffers[process_index]`, including on the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive()` (which calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). That necessarily discards any in-memory state previously held by the old `SpansBuffer` instance for those shards while `submit()` continues to call `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` on the (now new) buffers. However, the finding’s claimed consequences (counter drops, inability to distinguish unhealthy storms vs drift) depend on `SpansBuffer` internals and how its counters are used, which are not shown in the diff, so it’s a concrete but not provably correctness-breaking concern based solely on this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `break` on `remaining_time <= 0` in flusher.py:330-345 exits the loop before `process.terminate()` runs for the current process, so flusher processes still alive past the deadline are never terminated; on shutdown, remaining spawn processes leak, keep polling Redis, hold Redis connections, and potentially double-produce segments after the consumer is replaced by a restart.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop checks `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and does `break` when `remaining_time <= 0` *before* reaching the per-process `while process.is_alive()` wait and the subsequent `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. This means once the deadline is exceeded, the method exits the loop and skips terminating the current (and any remaining) multiprocessing flusher processes, leaving them running past shutdown. That behavior is directly implied by the diff at the new join-loop logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In `_ensure_processes_alive` restart path (flusher.py:244-262), the killed process is never `join()`ed before `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten, so SIGKILLed spawn processes become zombies until the parent reaps them, leaving one unreaped process per restart cycle over MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the restart path kills a `multiprocessing.Process` (`process.kill()`) and immediately starts a replacement via `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, overwriting `self.processes[process_index]` without ever calling `process.join()` (or otherwise waiting/reaping) on the killed process. The same pattern appears in `join()` where `process.terminate()` is called without a subsequent `join()`. This can leak OS process resources (zombie/unreaped children) across restarts/shutdowns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In flusher.py:57, `max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `flusher_processes=0` (or negative values) as falsy, so an operator passing `--flusher-processes 0` silently gets one process per shard with no validation or warning.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the diff sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This means an explicit `max_processes=0` (e.g. via the newly added `--flusher-processes` click option) will be treated as falsy and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, resulting in one process per shard instead of honoring the operator-provided value or raising/validating. The diff adds no validation on the click option or in `SpanFlusher` to prevent/handle 0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hot-path Redis-call multiplication in submit (flusher.py:267-269): `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` now fan out to one call per shard-buffer per submit instead of one call total, increasing per-message latency linearly with the number of flusher processes.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()` the diff changes single-buffer calls to per-buffer fan-out: `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` becomes `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `memory_infos = list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` becomes aggregating `buffer.get_memory_info()` across all buffers. Since `self.buffers` is keyed by `process_index` (one per flusher process/shard group), this makes `submit()` do work proportional to the number of flusher buffers/processes. The diff doesn’t prove these are Redis calls, but it does verify the linear fan-out and potential per-message latency increase introduced by the change, which is a concrete performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Metric tag inconsistency and unbounded cardinality (flusher.py:181-207): `produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use tag key `shard` while `wait_produce` uses `shards`, and the value is the joined shard list, breaking dashboards and creating combinatorial cardinality that inflates metric storage.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff shows `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses a different tag key (`shards`). Also, `shard_tag` is computed as a comma-joined list of shard ids (`",".join(map(str, shards))`), which can create high/unbounded tag-value cardinality depending on shard-to-process grouping. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability issue but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead/shadowed code path: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` (flusher.py:112-120) is never invoked anywhere — all call sites use `_create_process_for_shards` directly — and will diverge from the real path if mapping semantics change; it can be deleted with zero behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` (flusher.py) but no call sites in the shown changes invoke it. All restarts/creation paths go through `_create_processes()` and `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` (e.g., `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards`). Keeping an unused helper is dead/shadowed code and a maintenance risk if semantics change, but it does not introduce incorrect runtime behavior by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead guard in flusher.py:234-236: `if not process: continue` can never fire since Process/Thread objects are always truthy, misleading readers and silently skipping health checks for a process lost from `self.processes`, whose shards stop being flushed with no `flusher_unhealthy` metric emitted.

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the guard `if not process: continue` is likely dead because `self.processes` is populated with `Process`/`Thread` objects in `_create_process_for_shards` and never assigned `None` in this diff. However, the finding’s claimed impact (“silently skipping health checks for a process lost from `self.processes` … no metric emitted”) is not supported by the diff: if a process were “lost from `self.processes`” (missing key), the loop wouldn’t see it at all, and the `if not process` branch wouldn’t be involved. So the described bug scenario is not verifiable from the changes shown.
